summary: FireHistory Atlas is a web app that combines NASA MODIS and VIIRS historical active-fire detections into one consistent burning-activity calendar for the California area (2015 to 2021). Because the two sensors detect fires at different resolutions, raw counts cannot be compared directly. We use grid cell-day occurrence and total fire radiative power, plus an overlap-period comparison, to make the record fairer to read. Users can explore seasonal patterns, find unusually active periods and understand sensor differences. It is a historical tool, not a prediction system.
details: FireHistory Atlas lets users browse a calendar heatmap and a map of observed hotspot detections for the California area from 2015 to 2021. A Python pipeline standardizes timestamps and confidence fields from NASA MODIS and VIIRS S-NPP files, snaps detections to a 0.25 degree grid, and computes daily fire cell-days and total fire radiative power. It compares VIIRS with MODIS over the overlap period: in our data VIIRS reported a median of 3.49 times more raw detections than MODIS per month, 2.40 times more fire cell-days and 0.66 times the total fire power. It flags unusual days against a same-time-of-year baseline built from the median and median absolute deviation, and groups them into ranked periods. The strongest periods (September and October 2020, December 2017) are consistent with well-known California fire events, and both sensors agree on their timing. The front end is a static page using HTML, JavaScript and Leaflet, hosted on GitHub Pages. A permanent notice and the sensor notes explain that hotspots are satellite detections of thermal anomalies, not confirmed fires and not predictions. Tools: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Leaflet, Google Colab, GitHub Pages.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS MODIS Collection 6.1 and VIIRS S-NPP active-fire detections (Standard Processing archive), for a rectangle around California, 2 January 2015 to 29 December 2021. We used the location, date, time, confidence, type and fire radiative power fields.
